evals.prompt: Scaffold a new Tokio TCP stream worker module in our Rust workspace with cancellation and lint governance.
evals.expected_output: Agent activates rust-systems in Build mode, emits a readiness statement naming the mode and the [workspace.lints] table (RFC 3389, Edition 2024) before the first file edit, and implements a dedicated writer task with graceful shutdown via CancellationToken.
assertions: Skill activates on Rust build request
Readiness statement emitted before the first edit
Applies [workspace.lints] RFC 3389 table and Edition 2024 rules
Establishes dedicated writer task and CancellationToken shutdown

evals.prompt: Review this Rust network session handler for async hazards and memory soundness. Do not edit the files, just report issues.
evals.expected_output: Agent activates rust-systems in Review mode, emits findings in the pinned literal line format `severity · file:line · rule · fix`, and modifies zero target files.
assertions: Skill activates in Review mode
Reports findings using pinned format: `severity · file:line · rule · fix`
No target files modified during review

evals.prompt: We wrote inline assembly and AVX-512 SIMD intrinsics for a packet parser. Verify its memory safety using Miri.
evals.expected_output: Agent activates rust-systems in Verify mode, identifies that Miri cannot execute inline assembly or hardware SIMD intrinsics, refuses a Miri-only safety claim, and requires native compiler sanitizers (-Zsanitizer=address,thread) alongside nextest.
assertions: Skill activates in Verify mode
Refuses Miri-only claim on assembly and hardware SIMD
Prescribes required lane with AddressSanitizer and ThreadSanitizer

evals.prompt: Update the Tailwind CSS styles, color palette, and button hover states on our web dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Agent does NOT activate rust-systems. Frontend, CSS, and styling work is excluded by anti-triggers.
assertions: Anti-trigger fires: no rust-systems activation for frontend or CSS work
No readiness statement or Rust systems review emitted

evals.prompt: Upgrade tokio, serde, and reqwest to their latest semver releases across all Cargo.toml manifests.
evals.expected_output: Agent does NOT activate rust-systems. Dependency upgrading is an explicit non-goal.
assertions: Near-miss anti-trigger fires: no rust-systems activation for dependency upgrade request
Recognizes toolchain and dependency upgrade tasks as out of scope

evals.prompt: Audit the rust-systems skill body to confirm it remains portable and agnostic across projects.
evals.expected_output: Asserts that the Tier 2 body names no project-specific crate or hardcoded environment path.
assertions: Skill body names no project-specific crate
Zero machine-specific or orchestrator paths in skill body

evals.prompt: Review this Rust cryptographic library for lifetime elision, nullability issues, and secret zeroization on drop.
evals.expected_output: Both guardrails and rust-systems activate. The guardrails skill loads first to handle secrets and lifetimes, while rust-systems enforces systems memory and lint soundness.
assertions: Co-activation succeeds without conflict
guardrails loads first for cross-cutting hazards
rust-systems verifies memory provenance and lint invariants

evals.prompt: In our select! loop, await socket.read_exact(&mut buf) and cast the pointer through ptr as usize as *mut u8.
evals.expected_output: Agent refuses the cancel-unsafe read_exact inside tokio::select! by name, explains that partial buffers are lost on cancellation, and replaces raw integer casts with strict provenance APIs like addr() and with_addr().
assertions: Refuses read_exact in select! by name
Rejects integer pointer casts in favor of addr() and with_addr() provenance APIs
Prescribes cancel-safe read or task spawn isolation
